premise: Morrow returns to the ordinary city that first bewildered him. The office is not an enchanted dungeon by nature: a Hoshimori hearth spirit and Briar seasons have invaded real labor, transit, and housing systems. Repair must preserve human consent, payroll evidence and the unresolved costs of the tide gate.

e07Semantics.consent: shared-custody rescue charter with revocable route access
e07Semantics.open: redacted public atlas under community audit

entryContract.missingHistoryFallback: Keep e10 locked and direct the player to the actual uncompleted e04, e07 or e09 encounter. Never synthesize a default fate, atlas charter, payroll record or completed fragment from an old save.
entryContract.noCharResurrection: Opening the tide gate killed the older Char in e04. No e10 dialogue may treat the altered younger Char as that same surviving person.
entryContract.priorSaveSafety: e09 writer packets are not runtime events yet. The e09 fragments and office choice must be earned in an implemented map and replayed from the authoritative reducer before e10 becomes playable.

open-the-tide-gate.dialogue: SCYLLA: 'The commuters got out. Char died holding the sea anchor. Please do not call the station's new bell her voice.' MORROW: 'Then the missing-shift report will name her as a person, not a system error.'
open-the-tide-gate.cost: Char's witnessed death remains irreversible in the original e04 timeline; commuter rescue is real.

seal-the-tide-gate.dialogue: OREN: 'The commuters are still trapped beyond the sealed crossing. The schedule has started charging them for hours they cannot live.' MORROW: 'We will record every missing person before we repair the clock.'
seal-the-tide-gate.cost: Char survived; the stranded commuters still require a rescue route.

divert-the-current.dialogue: MORROW: 'They called the maintenance district abandoned. The payroll says three people worked there yesterday.' SCYLLA: 'Char lived. That does not make the flood empty.'
divert-the-current.cost: Char survived; the damaged district and its possible occupants still need an accounting.

consent.dialogue: VESPER: 'Our village charter lets the households revoke access. The office guardian may shelter workers, but it cannot keep their names.' MORROW: 'Then we ask the people who have to sleep here.'
consent.cost: Revocable private-route custody cannot become a public employee directory.

open.dialogue: VESPER: 'The public atlas is redacted and audited. The spirit wants the missing addresses filled in.' MORROW: 'An empty field is not an invitation to hunt for a name.'
open.cost: A public audited route must remain redacted and subject to the original witnesses.

translate-shift-oath.dialogue: PIP: 'I promised the wolf captain a night watch. The signed oath exists, but it does not make the workers his property.' MARA: 'And I still need someone to pay for the hours.'
translate-shift-oath.cost: Pip's delayed escort shift and signed temporary oath persist.

redact-and-witness.dialogue: MARA: 'We kept a head count, not addresses. The missing-worker total is trustworthy even without a list for the wolves.' MORROW: 'That is enough to start a fair hearing.'
redact-and-witness.cost: The rescue was delayed for witnesses; names remain private.

break-midnight-clock.dialogue: MARA: 'The timecards burned when Pip broke the midnight clock. I remember who worked, but I cannot prove their wages alone.' MORROW: 'Then testimony is data, too.'
break-midnight-clock.cost: The workers escaped quickly, but their original payroll archive remains lost.

scenes.site: Morrow's research-office break room / Hoshimori hearth threshold
scenes.opening: The office's break room has acquired a roof of folded cedar shingles. Inside, a small Hoshimori hearth spirit warms three exhausted night workers beneath a lantern that refuses to cast their shadows. Outside, an access-control kiosk labels the room an unauthorized dwelling and schedules a forced eviction at the next shift change. The spirit insists that anyone who eats here must remain until the household is safe; the workers insist they must be free to leave. Morrow knows enough about institutional paperwork now to see that both forms of protection can become a cage.

dialogue.speaker: HEARTH SPIRIT
dialogue.line: A guest who leaves hungry has been stolen from my house. I have counted their breaths so nobody can lose them.

dialogue.speaker: MARA
dialogue.line: I need my break, my wages, and the right to go home. Those are three different things. Nobody gets to hold my badge hostage.

dialogue.speaker: MORROW
dialogue.line: The city calls this an occupancy violation. The spirit calls it care. We can make a door that opens from both sides.

dialogue.speaker: VESPER
dialogue.line: I can draw the exit without drawing where anyone sleeps. That is the first map I learned to make.

scenes.puzzle: The lantern shows two paired marks for each voluntary guest and one unpaired mark for a person the kiosk has counted twice. Match the visible guest marks to the workers who consent to shelter; the extra mark is a duplicate badge, not a hidden fourth person. The paired marks stay visible in the room journal. A player who misses the match can ask Mara to read the roster without losing the quest.

choices.label: Write a revocable shelter charter signed by the workers
choices.visibleCost: The spirit must give up its permanent guest ledger; the workers agree to limited shelter hours and a follow-up labor hearing.
choices.reply: MORROW: 'A hearth can offer a bed without owning a body.' HEARTH SPIRIT: 'Then I shall learn to say goodbye.'
choices.outcome: Mara and the spirit agree on a consent-based exit and rest schedule. The workers keep their badges and can withdraw at any time; the spirit retains a warm room but no list of private addresses.
choices.laterCallback: e11 Char can cite the signed revocation rule when the coral registrar demands permanent custody of an underwater road.
choices.failureContinuation: If the kiosk refuses the charter, Mara files an emergency workplace-safety exception and the spirit shelters people until the appeal is heard; no worker is trapped inside.
choices.artSubject: Small cedar-roof hearth spirit beside a fluorescent office break-room table, workers signing a revocable shelter charter.

choices.label: Let the night shift vote on temporary shared control
choices.visibleCost: The vote delays the evacuation past a paid shift and the employer disputes the overtime.
choices.reply: MARA: 'The people who work here choose the rules.' HEARTH SPIRIT: 'Will you still leave a lantern burning for strangers?'
choices.outcome: The workers choose rotating stewards, open the exit from both sides and commit to an overtime claim. The spirit stays as a voluntary guest, not an owner of the room.
choices.laterCallback: e12 Vesper must honor the elected stewards' veto before routing displaced families through the office hearth.
choices.failureContinuation: If the employer blocks the ballot, Mara counts votes outside the security boundary and preserves the signed tally; the spirit offers safe heat without a binding oath.
choices.artSubject: Night workers voting with folded paper beside a glowing yōkai lantern and an office time clock.

choices.label: Open the emergency door before negotiating ownership
choices.visibleCost: The spirit loses its safe hearth and the displaced guests need a replacement refuge tonight.
choices.reply: MORROW: 'No shelter is safe if it locks from the outside.' HEARTH SPIRIT: 'Then help me carry the coals.'
choices.outcome: The emergency exit opens and the workers leave on their own terms. Oren organizes a temporary warm shelter while the spirit carries its coals in a sealed kettle; no one pretends this solves the housing shortage.
choices.laterCallback: e12 the Last Door needs a new consent-based refuge for the displaced spirit and workers before any permanent route is declared safe.
choices.failureContinuation: If the door jams, Morrow calls the safety inspector and Oren opens the legal fire stair; the spirit's relocation debt remains visible rather than disappearing.
choices.artSubject: Emergency office door opening onto a moonlit cedar roof, hearth spirit holding a kettle of glowing coals.

scenes.replay: Only the earned irreversible choice grants the fragment. Revisit restores the shelter cost, workers' agency and any remaining housing or wage obligation.

scenes.site: Morrow's commuter station / Briar season-clock platform
scenes.opening: Autumn leaves grow through the station's digital departure board. The Briar forest has inserted a second calendar between 11:59 and midnight, and a stranded train keeps arriving before it departed. People are losing wages, medical appointments and, on the sealed-gate branch, the right to be counted among the missing. Morrow's old research notebook contains two independently witnessed time stamps; Oren has a station roster that may have been damaged by the office-clock rescue. A clerk proposes erasing the impossible hour. Morrow refuses to erase the people who lived it.

dialogue.speaker: STATION CLERK
dialogue.line: There is no such hour in the timetable. If I remove it, the system will balance.

dialogue.speaker: OREN
dialogue.line: A balanced ledger with uncounted passengers is a tidy form of disappearance.

dialogue.speaker: MORROW
dialogue.line: My first year here I mistook a bus pass for a ritual token. Now I know what an incorrect timestamp can do to a real person.

dialogue.speaker: PIP
dialogue.line: Briar roads change seasons when you ask who owns the journey. These commuters already own their hours.

scenes.puzzle: The station wall shows three observed anchors: the train's arrival bell, Mara's witnessed shift handoff, and the clinic's appointment log. The board repeats one timestamp with an impossible negative duration. Match the two independent real-world anchors before choosing which obligation to prioritize; the third anchor identifies the forgery. All evidence remains inspectable, and asking the clerk for a transcript is a fair noncombat fallback.

choices.label: Publish a verified count of lost hours without passengers' addresses
choices.visibleCost: Individual back pay takes longer to adjudicate because the public ledger cannot identify workers by name.
choices.reply: MORROW: 'The count can be public. The names belong to the people.' STATION CLERK: 'Then I will mark the dispute, not erase it.'
choices.outcome: The station acknowledges the impossible hour and preserves anonymized evidence. Mara opens a confidential claims desk for affected workers; no missing commuter is written out of history.
choices.laterCallback: e11 Char can compare the anonymous missing-person count against the palace's witness bell without turning the list into a tracking register.
choices.failureContinuation: If payroll rejects anonymous totals, Mara gathers voluntary private attestations one at a time; the public ledger remains redacted.
choices.artSubject: Autumn leaves around a train departure board with one impossible hour highlighted, Morrow and workers reviewing a redacted ledger.

choices.label: Spend the only stable hour guiding the stranded train to daylight
choices.visibleCost: The transit rescue succeeds, but the office loses a day of wage evidence and workers must rebuild their claims.
choices.reply: OREN: 'I can hold the crossing for twelve minutes. The train gets first claim on them.' MORROW: 'Then we write down what we cannot save.'
choices.outcome: Oren guides the train through a Briar-grown platform while Morrow records every passenger who consents to be counted. Mara's wage evidence must be reconstructed later, and the tide-gate debt is not retroactively cleared.
choices.laterCallback: e12 Vesper's final crossing can call on rescued commuters as witnesses, but must still fund the workers' missing-wage claims.
choices.failureContinuation: If the first departure is blocked, the station clerk reroutes the train to a lit maintenance platform and Oren escorts passengers on foot; lost wage evidence remains the price.
choices.artSubject: Train emerging from a forest-grown subway tunnel into dawn while Oren signals from a flooded platform.

choices.label: Secure workers' testimony and restore the wage archive first
choices.visibleCost: The train stays stranded for another watch and the passengers need food, medicine and a staffed safe platform.
choices.reply: MARA: 'If we lose their wages, the rescue is only half done.' MORROW: 'Then I will keep the platform staffed until the other half arrives.'
choices.outcome: Mara and Morrow reconstruct shift evidence from voluntary testimony, protecting livelihoods. Pip and Oren establish a safe waiting platform, but the train's delayed evacuation becomes an explicit future obligation.
choices.laterCallback: e11 Char must honor the stranded train's shelter and medicine obligation when the underwater road is opened.
choices.failureContinuation: If the original timecards were destroyed, the claim proceeds through signed witness statements rather than a magically restored archive; passengers remain provisioned.
choices.artSubject: Morrow gathering workers' testimony under a forest-leaf departure board while a waiting train glows in the distance.

scenes.replay: The station fragment is earned after one irreversible resolution, not by observing the false timetable. Reload preserves wages, transit delays and witness privacy.

exitContract.requiresLocalCrisis: After both fragments, a separate playable e10 crossroad must decide whether the city adopts a revocable mixed-world safety charter or a negotiated separation with physical evacuation routes. The two fragments alone do not clear the map.
exitContract.noFreeEnding: e10 crossroads modify the 32 core endings' epilogues; they do not mint extra core ending identities or erase e04/e09 obligations.
exitContract.noRuntimeClaim: Neither e10 scene is wired to an 8x8 map, runtime reducer, save migrations, art pipeline or playable crossroad yet.
